correctness.rationale: The determinant perturbation identity proves p_i=λ_i e_{k-1}(λ_{-i})/e_k(λ); pairwise subtraction proves spectral order. For fixed extreme λ_1=1, λ_N=κ, Newton log-concavity makes µ decrease and χ increase in each intermediate eigenvalue, locating all four unique nondegenerate endpoints. Explicit positive diagonal matrices and least-eigenvalue error vectors attain the limits. One-step Euclidean error decomposition and an exact linear threshold inequality establish the block-budget corollary. Exact-arithmetic verification passed 153,536 assertions on 5,704 spectra; independent rotated-matrix projector reconstruction passed 972 assertions with <3e-15 Frobenius disagreement. Finite checks are supporting, not universal proofs.

value.rationale: Only the condition number is often available before committing to expensive determinantal blocks. The sharp one-step mean-square reduction certificate and necessary-and-sufficient block budget quantify a genuine algorithmic design trade-off, while the full χ range explains how strongly volume sampling can equalize spectra. The two different extremal multiplicity-one Gram profiles reveal distinct obstacles for contraction and transformed spectral conditioning. This is a motivated all-dimensional extremal classification, not a small isolated parameter improvement or computational lookup.
